summary:
NOVA MEDICA is an offline holographic health assistant for astronauts, built for the Brazilian Space Agency’s challenge on health monitoring for crews. On a mission to Mars there is no doctor on board, and a radio message takes up to about 20 minutes one way. Astronauts are not physicians, but they will be the first to act.

Once opened online for the first time, our app is cached and works without internet. It answers three questions. How am I doing? A 3D body scanner colors organs by status, backed by vitals and trends. What should I measure? Guided steps for seven vitals show the normal range and what to do if a value is off. Something happened, what now? Emergency Mode leads a crewmate through a triage tree with voice prompts, a timer and a CPR metronome.

It matters because crews need to act safely on their own while Earth is far away. Every status explains itself, and a summary can be exported for the doctor on Earth.
details:
What it does. A rules engine checks each reading against environment thresholds, the person’s own baseline, trends and combined signals (for example high pulse, low SpO2 and chest pain together), and explains every status in plain language. Four environments (ISS, Orion, Moon base, Mars transit) change thresholds, risks, reminders and communication delay. A Databank covers the NASA Human Research Program hazards, a Health Score and reminders support daily routine, and Ground Link exports a summary in JSON or PDF for a doctor on Earth. A deterministic simulator provides normal, slow-drift and collapse scenarios, so the demo is repeatable.

Benefits and impact. Crews get fast self-checks, clear next steps and guided first aid when a crewmate collapses and panic is high. The same offline approach could help remote communities on Earth with limited access to medical care.

Tools. TypeScript, React, three.js with React Three Fiber, Zustand, Recharts, Zod, Vite, Bun, jsPDF, IndexedDB, Web Audio and Speech Synthesis. The app is a PWA and all medical content lives in JSON files.

Creativity. A holographic scanner with a scan beam, organs that change color with status, a heart that pulses at the real heart rate, and an emergency interface designed for a stressed non-expert: one question per screen, large buttons, no reliance on color alone.

What we considered. Offline-first design, because space has no internet. Honesty: the app does not diagnose. It only estimates urgency and follows a protocol. Microgravity changes what is normal, so each reading is also compared with the person’s own baseline.

Disclaimer: demonstration prototype. Not a medical device and does not replace a doctor. All data is simulated.
